text: The applicants are Hungarian nationals.
The first applicant was born in 1943.
The second applicant was born in 1945.
The third applicant was born in 1951.
The applicants live in Budapest.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 1 December 2002 the Romanian Prime Minister made an official visit to Budapest.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 1 December 2002 the Romanian Prime Minister gave a reception in Budapest on the occasion of Romania's national day.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Romania's national day commemorates the 1918 Gyulafehérvár National Assembly.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The 1918 Gyulafehérvár National Assembly was the occasion when the transfer of hitherto Hungarian Transylvania to Romania was declared.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Hungarian Prime Minister decided to attend the reception given by the Romanian Prime Minister on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Hungarian Prime Minister made his intention to attend the reception public the day before the event, i.e. on 30 November 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants were of the opinion that the Hungarian Prime Minister should refrain from attending the reception given by the Romanian Prime Minister on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants considered the Gyulafehérvár National Assembly to have negative significance in Hungarian history.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants decided to organise a demonstration in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest where the reception was to be held.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants did not inform the police of their intention to organise a demonstration in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: In the afternoon of 1 December 2002, approximately 150 people assembled in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants were among the approximately 150 people who assembled in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The police were present at the assembly in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: There was a loud noise during the assembly in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The police decided to disband the assembly in front of the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest, considering that it constituted a risk to the security of the reception.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The police forced the demonstrators back to a park next to the Hotel Kempinski in Budapest.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: After being forced to the park next to the Hotel Kempinski, the demonstrators dispersed after a while.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 16 December 2002 the applicants sought judicial review of the action of the police before the Pest Central District Court.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants requested the Pest Central District Court to declare the police action of disbanding the assembly on 1 December 2002 unlawful.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants asserted before the Pest Central District Court that the demonstration on 1 December 2002 had been totally peaceful.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants asserted before the Pest Central District Court that the only aim of the demonstration on 1 December 2002 had been to express their opinion.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants pointed out that it had obviously been impossible to inform the police about the assembly three days in advance, as required by Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act), because the Hungarian Prime Minister had only announced his intention to attend the reception the day before the event.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 6 February 2003 the Pest Central District Court dismissed the applicants' action seeking judicial review of the police action of disbanding the assembly on 1 December 2002.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court noted that the demonstration on 1 December 2002 had been disbanded after a minor detonation was heard.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court noted that the three-day time-limit for informing the police of a planned assembly could not possibly be observed if the demonstration had its roots in an event that had occurred less than three days beforehand.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court was of the view that the possible shortcomings of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) could not be remedied by the courts.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court held that the duty to inform the police about assemblies applied to every type of demonstration, including spontaneous ones.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court noted that there might be a need for more precise and sophisticated regulations in respect of spontaneous assemblies but said that this was a task for the legislator, not the courts.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court found that the duty to inform the police in advance about assemblies held in public served to protect the public interest and the rights of others, namely the free flow of traffic and the right to freedom of movement.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court observed that the organisers of the demonstration on 1 December 2002 had not even attempted to notify the police.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court stated that under the relevant provisions of Hungarian domestic law in force, the fact that an assembly is peaceful is not by itself enough to dispense with the duty to inform the police.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court stated that it had not dealt with the issue of whether or not the assembly on 1 December 2002 was peaceful, since the lack of notification made it illegal per se.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Pest Central District Court stated that the police had dissolved the assembly on 1 December 2002 lawfully, pursuant to section 14(1) of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act).
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants appealed against the Pest Central District Court's decision of 6 February 2003.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 16 October 2003 the Budapest Regional Court upheld the first-instance decision of the Pest Central District Court of 6 February 2003.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Regional Court amended part of the Pest Central District Court's reasoning by omitting the remarks concerning the possible shortcomings of the relevant domestic law.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Regional Court referred, inter alia, to the case-law of the European Court of Human Rights and to decision no. 55/2001 (XI. 29.) of the Hungarian Constitutional Court.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Regional Court found that in the application of the relevant domestic law, there is no exemption from the duty of notification and therefore no difference between 'notified' assemblies and 'spontaneous' ones, the latter being unlawful owing to the failure to respect the duty of notification.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Budapest Regional Court found that the restrictions imposed on the applicants were necessary and proportionate.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The applicants lodged a petition for review with the Hungarian Supreme Court.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: On 24 February 2004 the Hungarian Supreme Court dismissed the applicants' petition for review without examining its merits.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: The Hungarian Supreme Court dismissed the applicants' petition for review because it was incompatible ratione materiae with the relevant provisions of the Hungarian Code of Civil Procedure.
section_path: A.  The circumstances of the case

text: Article 62 of the Hungarian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of peaceful assembly.
Article 62 of the Hungarian Constitution secures the free exercise of the right to freedom of peaceful assembly.
Section 6 of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) requires the police to be informed of an assembly at least three days before the date of the event.
Section 14(1) of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) requires the police to disband any assemblies held without prior notification.
Section 14(3) of Law no. III of 1989 on the right of assembly (the Assembly Act) provides that if an assembly is dissolved its participants may seek judicial review within fifteen days.
